verdict.rationale: Tailscale documents its own webhooks, which automatically notify a receiving endpoint when tailnet events occur, and it lists webhooks among its tailnet automation options. That is an event-triggered action the product itself provides, but there is no evidence of a rules engine that lets users define conditions and run arbitrary actions inside Tailscale. Community examples, such as a Slack bot that updates ACLs, are user-built workarounds and earn no credit. missing for 10: user-definable event-to-action rules within the product, documented trigger conditions/filters, built-in action types beyond notification, independent hands-on corroboration.
